reason: 68 MiB of prebuilt per-target flash images for the browser-based ESP Web Tools flasher. Verified re-obtainable from two independent places: the pinned repo commit, and this project's GitHub Releases, which publish the same per-target assets for every version tag.
notes: `firmware-s3.bin` is a **merged full-flash image**, exactly 8,388,608 B (8 MiB) — mostly erased padding, which is why the directory is so large. SHA-256 `d2b8fe67e3f6310cb74e9e02b8afd60acff63495bbea8aab33ab53a0198f631b`, chip ID 9 = ESP32-S3, DIO / 8 MB / 80 MHz.
`firmware.bin` is the **ESP32-C6** merged image (4,194,304 B, chip ID 13, DIO / 4 MB / 40 MHz) — despite the unqualified name it is *not* the S3 build.

The versioned `firmware-app-*-1.10.0 … 1.22` files are historical per-release application images. Example: `firmware-app-c5-1.10.0.bin` is an **ESP32-C5** (chip ID 23) app built **2026-03-31 11:44:16** against **ESP-IDF v5.5.4**, project `arduino-lib-builder`, ELF SHA-256 `3080fb06…`.
These are build outputs, but ESP-IDF builds are **not byte-reproducible**, so rebuilding from source will not recreate these exact bytes. They are preserved rather than discarded for that reason.
Not needed to read, understand or build the project — the firmware source is retained in the repository.
verification: Checked against upstream 2026-08-24: the same assets are published under GitHub Releases v1.10.0 through v1.22, giving a second recovery path independent of the git object store.
